Warn or block distracting apps during a focus
Focus works entirely offline. It has no account, no ads, no analytics and no permission to use the internet. Everything you record stays on this device.

Your focus sessions (start and end time, duration, whether it was completed, subject, task, rating and note), your subjects, tasks, goals, routine and reviews, your settings, achievements progress and the list of apps you chose to avoid. This data is kept in the app\'s private storage on your device. It is not included in Android cloud backups or device transfers.

If you turn on app blocking and allow Usage access, Focus checks which app is in the foreground, only while a focus is running, to compare it with your list. The result is used at that moment and is never recorded, stored or sent anywhere.
If you choose block mode and allow it, Focus uses this permission only to show its own block screen over an app from your list during a focus.
To let you pick apps to avoid, Focus reads the list of apps that appear in your launcher. The list is shown to you on the device and not stored, except for the apps you select.
Focus uses notifications for the running timer, the end of each phase, unlocked achievements and focus reminders. They are created on the device.
When you export your progress, Focus creates an encrypted file in the place you choose. Only Focus can read it. You decide where it goes and with whom you share it.
Focus does not share any data with the developer or third parties. You can delete your history at any time in Settings, and uninstalling the app removes all of its data.

Focus is not directed at children under 13. If this policy changes, the new version is shipped with an app update and its effective date is updated. Questions: use the contact e-mail on the app\'s Google Play page.
Reminders may arrive up to a few minutes late: Focus does not use exact alarms, which saves battery.
